patch.format: unified diff, exactly three context lines

qom_property.name: cache-port
qom_property.meaning: Controller port role, not a PSRAM-ready/enable flag; set before realize.

system_clock_link.name: system-clock
system_clock_link.spi1: Leave unlinked for unchanged existing PIO semantics.
system_clock_link.gate_rule: perip_clk_en0 bit1 set, perip_rst_en0 bit1 clear and existing pll_valid true for the selected PLL-derived80MHz MSPI source
system_clock_link.register_write_rule: While perip_rst_en0 bit1 is held, all SPI0 writes return MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR and leave fields unchanged. Clock-off configuration writes/readback remain available.

controller.bus_ownership: SPI1 CS1 owns the sole 8 MiB SsiPsramState and byte-SSI bus attachment. SPI0 cache service never allocates a PSRAM chip or independently transacts its empty SSI bus.
controller.unsupported_spi0_pio: Nonzero write to SPI_MEM_CMD returns MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR via write_with_attrs; zero write is harmless. SPI1 forwards to its original PIO callback.
controller.spi1_preservation: All added register read/write/reset behavior is guarded by cache_port. Existing SPI1 flash/XTS transaction paths remain unchanged beyond the separately owned two-index transport fix.
controller.undefined_registers: No general register-array/write-echo fallback; original unsupported-register behavior remains.

api.effect: Pure eligibility predicate; no data transfer, mutation or allocation. Parent maps false to MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR for CPU cache and committed GDMA access.
common_rules: Non-null SPI0 cache-port and actual SSI PSRAM chip
8 MiB chip, non-octal, actual qpi=true, linear wrap32=false

Typed system-clock link required; SYSTEM_PERIP_CLK_EN0.SPI01_CLK_EN bit1=1, SYSTEM_PERIP_RST_EN0.SPI01_RST bit1=0 and existing pll_valid=true for the selected80MHz PLL-derived MSPI source. CLOCK_GATE.CLK_EN is register-clock force-on, not a functional gate; ordinaryIDF rtc_init clears it and both0/1 are operational.
SMEM_DDR bits30:24 and DDR_EN bit0 zero (no HyperBus/octal/DQS/differential/DDR)
CORE_CLK_SEL=0 and SRAM_CLK=0x00010001 for pinned 80 MHz core / 2 =40 MHz
read_rules: Effective read dummy clocks = RDUMMY_CYCLELEN+1 + (SMEM_TIMING_CALI.TIMING_CALI ? EXTRA_DUMMY_CYCLELEN : 0), exactly six
api.directionality: Read predicate does not require valid write command/dummy; write predicate does not require valid read command/dummy. Common address, mode and clock rules apply to both.

supported_modes.timing_claim: Functional register/phase eligibility, not waveform/analogue/latency accuracy. SRAM delay-mode/number/output timing fields read back with public masks; physical delay is not modeled.

unsupported_or_unknown_modes: SPI cache mode (including HAL SPI/DIO mapping): false; SPI1 byte-SSI PIO SPI transport remains available
DIO, OPI/octal, DDR, HyperBus, differential/DQS-enabled PSRAM cache: false
Unknown commands, command lengths, address widths, dummy counts, user-command bypasses: false
Other frequencies/core selections: false in this pinned cache qualification mode

setup_example.spi1_first: SSI command0x35 enters actual chip QPI before cache use
setup_example.smem_ddr_default: 0x00003020 at0xe4; do not confuse with inherited flash DDR at0xe0

reset.interface: Existing soc-reset QOM link and ResettableClass hold callback; parent integrates SPI0 in existing SPI01 peripheral reset domain, with no fabricated clock/reset bits.
reset.realize: Install public SPI0 defaults after cache-port property assignment.
reset.periph_or_chip_controller_reset: Reset new SPI0 fields to public defaults, MISC=0, inherited flash DDR=0x00003020, CLOCK_GATE=1. Defaults do not qualify data access.
reset.level_held_spi01_reset: write_with_attrs rejects every SPI0 guest write with MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR while typed system-clock perip_rst_en0 bit1 remains asserted; valid fields cannot latch until reset release. Existing central SPI01 reset strobe resets the controller phases.
reset.cpu_only_reset: Existing PERIPH reset-domain guard retains controller phases.
reset.warm_external_chip: No SSI chip reset or allocation from SPI0; chip data/qpi persist under controller phase reset. Parent cache reset discards dirty CPU state separately.
reset.recovery: Reprogram valid phases/clock/CS1 to regain backing access; chip may already remain QPI.

required_by_main: Prepare NEW immutable candidate after phase patch and integration
Confirm proper patch application after frozen prefix and minimal SPI1 index fix
Build native candidate once and run owned qtests/ordinary pinned SDK firmware qualification
Exercise wrong phase/SSI mode/DDR/CS1 faults, correct reads and writes, committed GDMA view, and warm phase reset without losing chip data
